name: Dance tuition for kids
summary: How expat parents evaluate ballet, contemporary, hip-hop, and cultural dance schools in Singapore — trial classes, exam tracks (RAD/IDTA), and how dance CCAs interact with international-school schedules.
body:
Dance is one of the densest kids’ enrichment markets after swimming and Mandarin. Studios range from shopping-mall hip-hop chains to serious ballet schools with graded exams. Match the studio to your child’s goal before prepaying a year.

## Goal matching
- **Recreation / confidence** — fun combos, flexible make-ups for home leave
- **Graded ballet** — RAD/other syllabus, exam fees, progressive levels
- **Performance / company tracks** — higher hours, competition or showcase commitments
- **Cultural dance** — community groups tied to language/heritage identity

International-school calendars (travel weeks, IB deadlines) clash with rigid exam studios — ask about make-up policies before signing.

## Practical checks
Visit changing rooms and observation policies; confirm teacher-to-student ratios and first-aid norms. Floors, mirrors, and ventilation matter in humid weather. Costume fees for concerts can surprise — get the annual extras list in writing.

## How to choose
Prefer schools that let you trial before package payment and that separate marketing “elite” labels from actual syllabus progression. For boys or late starters, ask about inclusive class placement rather than age-only stigma. Older teens aiming for GCSE/IB dance need syllabus-aware teachers, not only commercial choreography.

## Practical tip
Schedule dance on days that do not stack after heavy academic tuition. Overuse injuries show up fast in growth spurts — pair serious hours with sensible rest and, if needed, sports medicine rather than “dance through pain” culture.
